constraints.decision: Purpose: The user has so many files in their Downloads folder that they cannot find the one they are looking for; they want the files grouped by type (images, documents, archives and so on) so they can find them.

What grouping does to files: The tool moves files into a folder per type (such as Images, Documents, Archives) made inside the Downloads folder. Only the files directly in the Downloads folder are its targets. It only moves: it never deletes, renames or overwrites a file. Run plainly, it only shows what it would move where; it moves files only when told to. Where the target folder already holds a file of the same name, that file is left where it is and reported.
Computers it runs on: The tool must work on macOS and Linux; working on Windows too is welcome but not required.

Types and files of no type: A file's type is told by its file-name extension, in a fixed set of groups: Images, Documents, Archives, Audio, Video and Installers (such as .dmg, .pkg, .deb). A file with no extension, or one no group holds, is not moved and is left where it is, shown in a list. Which extensions each group holds is still to be settled.

How the finished work is checked: The finished work is checked on a test folder of made-up files, not on the user's real Downloads folder; the user tries the finished work themselves on a made-up Downloads folder to confirm it. The work also gives a README that says how to install and how to use the tool, and tests that check what has been decided for the tool.
Undoing the last run: The tool can undo its last run: undoing moves each file the last run moved back to where it was. The acceptance criteria and the tests check the undo too.
Which run undo reaches: Undo reaches only the last run that moved files; a run that only shows moves nothing and is not what undo undoes. Undoing runs before that one is not part of the work.

Files undo cannot move back: Where a file the last run moved cannot go back as it was, because a file of the same name is now in its old place or it is no longer in the group's folder, undo leaves it where it is and reports it by name, and moves every other file back; undo too never deletes, renames or overwrites a file.

Group folders on undo: Undo removes a group folder only where the last run made it and it is empty once the files are moved back; a folder that holds anything, or that was there before the last run, is left as it is.

Undo right after an undo: Undo undoes only a run that grouped files; run again right after an undo, with no grouping run since, it moves nothing and says there is no run to undo. To group the files again, the user runs the tool with the instruction to move.

UX document: A UX document is made, of kind ux, at .rn/20261030-downloads-organizer-cli/ux.md, kept in the session folder alone and not in what the work leaves, so the user approves how the tool is used and what it shows before it is built; it does not say again what the README says.

README: The tool's README, of kind readme, is written at downloads-organizer/README.md, in the tool's own folder downloads-organizer/, and the top README.md gains only one line pointing to it; the rest of the top README stays as it is.

Development document: A development document is made at downloads-organizer/docs/development.md, at the architecture or the build stage, for whoever builds or changes the tool: how its code is laid out, how to run its tests, and the way to its architecture; the README's Development section links to it. What it holds, and its kind, are still to be heard at that stage.
